text:
Anita V: quick pulse — we hit a hard GPU OOM in prod last night during a big rerank burst, runtime fell back to CPU but some tenants saw 10x latency spike. quick thread to capture followups.
Mike H: saw the alert, logs show KV cache thrash + pinned tensors preventing eviction. OOM happened after a sudden traffic spike from a single tenant.
Sara L: do we have a clear sequence of actions when OOM happens? fallback->migrate->recompute? the handoff is messy.
Ryan P: current flow: 1) detect OOM 2) runtime asks evictor for candidates 3) if eviction fails, fallback to CPU path. we don't have a guaranteed recovery handshake to free pinned or soft-reserved pages.
Anita V: that's the gap — no interface to ask tenant code to release ephemeral pins or checkpoint shard. we need a protocol between runtime and serving code.
Mike H: proposal: add an "oom_grace_cycle" callback to the allocator API. runtime sends a short async notice: "oom_warning(token, severity)". tenant handlers can eagerly drop caches or checkpoint tensors. if freed within window, runtime retries allocation.
Sara L: sounds reasonable. window size? 50-200ms? tradeoff: too small = no effect, too large = latency tails. maybe adaptive based on current SLO.
Ryan P: agree adaptive. also need a synchronous path for pinned pages by core runtime components (KV cache pinned by tokenizer model state) — these should be cooperative.
Mike H: sketch of API:
```cpp
// runtime -> allocator
bool oom_warning(uint64_t token, uint32_t severity_ms);
// allocator -> runtime
enum OomAction { RETRY, FORCE_EVICT, FALLBACK };
OomAction oom_response(uint64_t token, size_t reclaimed_bytes);
```
Runtime will wait up to severity_ms, then call oom_response to decide next step.
Anita V: nit: avoid large blocking waits on the main serving thread. implement as a short non-blocking handshake with a retry backoff loop.
Sara L: also need observable signals: metric oom_warning_count, average reclaimed_bytes, per-tenant warn latency. this will help tune defaults.
Ryan P: eviction policy tweak — prefer evicting unpinnable KV shards first, then compressible tensors, then soft-demote pinned tensors with graceful checkpointing. need an ordered action list with fallbacks.
Mike H: yes — policy should be a configurable chain. default chain for hosted: [kv-unpin, compress, soft-demote-checkpoint, fallback-cpu]. Enterprise can enable more aggressive FORCE_EVICT.
Anita V: what about recompute vs migration? for some activations, recompute is cheaper than migrating to CPU. runtime should know operator cost and recompute budget. we need an O(1) hint on tensor: recompute_cost_estimate.
Sara L: we can tag tensors at load time with metadata: {pinned:bool, recompute_cost:float, compressible:bool, checkpointable:bool}. this metadata informs eviction scorer.
Ryan P: acceptance tests: synthetic churn test that pins N tensors and bursts traffic, verify that oom_warning path reduces tail latency and doesn't drop requests. also chaos test where eviction callbacks sleep.
Mike H: rollout plan: 1) implement warning API + metrics behind feature flag, 2) add default eviction chain, 3) canary on dedicated pool, 4) enable hosted slowly and monitor oom_warning_count and latency tails.
Anita V: compatibility note: allocators must keep backward compat for older tenants. if allocator doesn't implement oom_warning, runtime falls back to existing behavior.
Sara L: security/tenancy note: warn messages must be scoped per-tenant; don't let tenant-side handlers affect other tenants. token is per-tenant and validated.
Ryan P: open question — should we allow tenant handlers to request that runtime preempt other low-priority tenants to free memory? feels risky for fairness. propose a policy bit: allow_cross_tenant_eviction (off by default).
Mike H: agreed off by default. enterprise customers can opt-in with explicit SLAs.
Anita V: small config example for runtime config:
```
memory_recovery:
  warning_window_ms: 120
  eviction_chain:
    - kv_unpin
    - compress
    - soft_demote
    - fallback_cpu
  allow_cross_tenant_eviction: false
```
Ryan P: test checklist: perf microbench for handshake overhead (<1% p99), integration with canary, metrics dashboard, run nemesis tests.
Sara L: I'll own metrics + dashboard. Mike, Ryan — you own API + evictor integration. Anita — you own rollout playbook.
Anita V: thanks. last: add a short RFC doc with sequence diagram and failure modes. I'll draft and ping for review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
evictor-bot: canary-deploy: memory-recovery-feature -> success on pool-dedicated-3 :white_check_mark:
Mike H: awesome, will start implementation today.
Sara L: adding observability tickets now.
Ryan P: will draft tests and a chaos script.
Anita V: closing thread — let's sync after first canary.
